notes: A LaTeX-typeset maths thesis (Baire-1 functions). Plain prose and references read correctly (2, 4-9, 17-20, 26, 28, 35-37). Almost every line with inline maths is misread, often with Latin maths italics turned into look-alike Greek letters: 'C_n'→'Γη' (10), 'n_0 ∈ ℕ'→'ηο Ε Ν' (11), 'U'/'x'→'υ'/'α' (13), 'Baire, ∃k_0'→'Βαιρε, Ξκο' (14), 'g'→'9' (16), 'b_j'/'x_1'→'δ;'/'χι' (21), 'δ_n'→'δη' (22), '∪_{n=1}^∞'→'U_1' (23), 'F'→'Ε' (29, 31), 'd_∞'→'do' (33), '⊆'→'C' (34, 38). These maths lines are about a third or more of only 71 admitted lines. They cannot be isolated by regex, because 'η' and 'ο' are also ordinary Greek articles and several bad lines carry no residue flag (10, 13, 14, 16), so dropping the whole small book is safer than keeping Latin→Greek confusions.
